artifacts.notes:
265 pages. Front matter runs i-v over artifact pages 2-7 and the body's printed
page 1 begins at artifact page 9, so a printed page number is normally eight
behind the artifact page; every passage record here states the artifact page,
which is what the bytes support, and gives the printed page beside it.
The text layer is clean and usable as a finding aid; it is not exact, and
transcription is from the page images.
One production defect worth knowing before a page reference is trusted: the
running head is wrong on parts of Holy Week -- artifact pages 42 and 44 are
headed LENT while sitting inside PALM SUNDAY OF THE PASSION OF THE LORD, which
begins at artifact page 40.

edition.authority: International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation, whose translation this is; delivered by the Liturgy Office of the Bishops' Conference of England and Wales
edition.jurisdiction: The universal ICEL English, common to ICEL's eleven member episcopal conferences. THE HOST IS NOT THE TERRITORY. The document carries no England-and-Wales adaptation, its own notices claim only Libreria Editrice Vaticana, ICEL and the Revised Grail, and its foreword cites the GIRM of the 2011 Roman Missal; the Liturgy Office is its delivery route and not its authority.
edition.notes:
THE FIRST ENGLISH EDITION LINE THIS WORK HAS HAD. All nine editions previously
recorded under work.catholic-church.missale-romanum are Latin. This one and its
sibling 2011-english-cbcew-excerpts are English, and they are directories named
with the date first, per guidance/sources.md, which the older Latin siblings
predate.

WHAT IT CONTAINS, from its own foreword at artifact page 6: "the English
translation of all the Entrance Antiphons and Communion Antiphons and various
other hymns, songs, responsories, and antiphons in the Missale Romanum,
2002/2008." Its table of contents runs the Proper of Time from Advent through
Ordinary Time, the Proper of Saints month by month, the Commons, ten Ritual
Masses, Various Needs and Occasions, Votive Masses, Masses for the Dead, and two
appendices -- the Rite for the Blessing and Sprinkling of Water and the Rite of
Blessing a Chalice and a Paten within Mass -- followed by an index of scripture
references, an alphabetical index of antiphons without scripture references, and
a psalm numbering chart. Psalm and canticle assignments taken from the Graduale
Romanum and Graduale Simplex are printed in red below the antiphons of Sundays
and major feasts; those are the compiler's assignments, not Missal text.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is an excerpt-compilation of the Missal's antiphons, made to
assist composers. It carries no orations, and it must never be cited as the
Missal itself or as a ritual edition.

THE RIGHTS ARE MIXED INSIDE ONE FILE and the mixing is the reason this edition
matters beyond its coverage. Its copyright page names three claimants: the Latin
to Libreria Editrice Vaticana 2008, the English translation to ICEL 2010, and
"the English translation of Psalms 23(24), 46(47), and 115(116) from The Revised
Grail Psalms (c) 2010 Conception Abbey/The Grail, administered by GIA
Publications, Inc." The artifact record and the passages below record where the
Grail text actually falls, which is a smaller and more precise place than the
notice alone would tell you.
edition.publication: A 265-page PDF whose title page reads ANTIPHONARY EXCERPTED FROM THE ROMAN MISSAL / RENEWED BY DECREE OF THE MOST HOLY SECOND ECUMENICAL COUNCIL OF THE VATICAN, PROMULGATED BY AUTHORITY OF POPE PAUL VI AND REVISED AT THE DIRECTION OF POPE JOHN PAUL II / ENGLISH TRANSLATION ACCORDING TO THE THIRD TYPICAL EDITION / 2010. Published free and entire by the Liturgy Office of the Bishops' Conference of England and Wales at https://www.liturgyoffice.org.uk/Missal/Music/Antiphonary.pdf, whose page describes it as "the ICEL Antiphonary" and adds that a Word version is available on request; state retrieved 2026-08-21.

passages.context:
The Rite of Blessing a Chalice and a Paten within Mass, in the appendices. Read
on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact page 242, printed page 234. No
liturgical text is transcribed into this record.

THE THIRD AND LAST GRAIL LOCUS IN THIS DOCUMENT, and the answer to a question
this repository had left open. The Antiphonary's copyright page reserves Psalms
23(24), 46(47) and 115(116) to The Revised Grail Psalms; the first two were found
on Palm Sunday and the third had not been located anywhere in this repository's
ledger. It is here. The rubric directs that "if appropriate, this antiphon with
Psalm 115 is sung"; a two-line ICEL antiphon follows, then the heading "Psalm
115" and the psalm printed in strophes with the antiphon repeated between them,
in the same construction as the two Palm Sunday procession antiphons.

Its neighbour in the appendices, the Rite for the Blessing and Sprinkling of
Water at artifact pages 240-241, prints NO psalm strophes and is clear of the
carve-out.

Everywhere else in the document Psalm 115 is either a red Graduale assignment --
"(Psalm 22[23] or Psalm 115: 10-19: GR, p. 170)" at the Mass of the Lord's
Supper, "(Psalm 21[22] ... or Psalm 115: 10-19: GR, p. 149)" on Palm Sunday, and
similar -- which is a citation and not Grail text; or an ICEL antiphon of the
Missal citing Ps 115: 15 or Ps 115: 12-13, which is ICEL's own translation of the
verse as an antiphon and not the Grail's psalter. The distinction is between a
psalm printed as a psalm and a verse translated as an antiphon, and only the
first is GIA's.
passages.notes: Established by enumerating every centred "Psalm N" heading in the retained bytes -- exactly three across 265 pages -- and then reading every occurrence of "Psalm 115" and "Ps 115" in context. This closes the open item recorded at guidance/liturgical-text-publication-policy.md section 5.1, which said Psalm 115(116) had not been located in this repository's ledger and should be before any Triduum antiphon is considered. It is not in a Triduum antiphon; it is in an appended ritual Mass.

passages.context:
The copyright page, read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact page 2,
the verso of the title page. Three notices and nothing else on the page:

"Latin text (c) Libreria Editrice Vaticana, Vatican City State, 2008."

"The English translation of The Roman Missal (c) 2010, International Commission
on English in the Liturgy Corporation. All rights reserved."

"The English translation of Psalms 23(24), 46(47), and 115(116) from The Revised
Grail Psalms (c) 2010 Conception Abbey/The Grail, administered by GIA
Publications, Inc., www.giamusic.com. All rights reserved."

THREE THINGS FOLLOW, and all three matter to a later lane.

There is no CBCEW claim on this page. The Liturgy Office hosts the file; the
document itself claims nothing for England and Wales, and its foreword cites the
GIRM of the 2011 Roman Missal. It is a witness to the universal ICEL English and
not to a national adaptation -- neither England and Wales's nor the United
States's.

The Grail claim is a different rightsholder's and ICEL's grant does not reach it.
The three psalms named are the same three the 2011 United States Missal's own
front matter names, per the notices recorded at
src/sources/inventories/lt-hist-rights-audit-v1.toml, so this is not a
United-States artefact: it is in the document this project would source from.

The acknowledgment form here is the plain "The English translation of The Roman
Missal" one, without "and chants". ICEL's own chant files carry the "translation
and chants" form. The notice travels with the file the words were read out of.
passages.notes: The notice names the psalms as 23(24), 46(47) and 115(116) -- Vulgate numbering first. The document's own psalm numbering chart at artifact page 265 gives the mapping, and its foreword states that its psalm references follow the Vulgate and Septuagint numbering.

passages.context:
The Foreword, read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact pages 6-7,
printed pages iv-v. It is the document's own statement of what it contains and
of the conventions a reader must know before citing a page of it.

Its opening sentence is the completeness claim this edition is registered for:
the Antiphonary "contains the English translation of all the Entrance Antiphons
and Communion Antiphons and various other hymns, songs, responsories, and
antiphons in the Missale Romanum, 2002/2008."

Six conventions are then stated, and four bear on how the document may be used
as a source.

Psalm and canticle assignments were made by the compiler "in order to assist
composers", for the antiphons "used on Sundays and major feasts and solemnities
of the liturgical year"; the reference "appears in red within parentheses below
the antiphon to which it has been assigned" and cites page numbers in the
Graduale Romanum (Tournai, 1974) and the Graduale Simplex. THESE ARE THE
COMPILER'S ASSIGNMENTS AND NOT MISSAL TEXT, and must not be carried into a
corpus as though the Missal had printed them.

Where two Communion Antiphons stand in one proper, "the second is usually from
one of the Gospels", and preference should usually be given to the one from the
Mass's own Gospel.

The indexes at printed pages 236-249 and 250-256 "identify those texts that are
repeated and direct the user to the day or occasion on which these texts are
sung" -- which is a ready-made map of the antiphons this Missal uses more than
once, and the right instrument for detecting a duplicate identity rather than
inferring one.

Psalm references follow "the Vulgate and Septuagint numbering", with a
Hebrew-Vulgate chart at printed page 257.

Also stated: "Where useful, rubrics from the Missal have been given in place for
a particular day, liturgical season, occasion, or section in the Missal in order
to provide a context for the use or selection of an antiphon." So some of what
this document prints in italic is Missal rubric and some is the compiler's
apparatus, and the two are not distinguished typographically in every case.
passages.notes: The foreword's footnotes cite the Ordo Cantus Missae (24 June 1974) and the GIRM "in the Third Typical Edition of The Roman Missal, 2011". The second is the strongest internal evidence that this document witnesses the universal 2010/2011 English rather than an England-and-Wales state.

passages.context:
Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord, the Commemoration of the Lord's Entrance
into Jerusalem, First Form: The Procession -- Antiphon 1 with its psalm and
Antiphon 2 with its psalm. Read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact
pages 41-42, printed pages 33-34. No liturgical text is transcribed into this
record; see the note below.

THIS IS THE EVIDENCE FOR THE REVISED GRAIL CARVE-OUT, seen rather than inferred.
Each of these two loci is one slot containing two rightsholders' property.

Antiphon 1, artifact page 41, is an ICEL antiphon of the Missal, four sense
lines, followed by the red assignment "(Psalm 23[24]: GR, p. 139)", the rubric
"If appropriate, this antiphon is repeated between the strophes of the following
Psalm", and then the heading "Psalm 23" with the whole psalm printed in five
strophes, each followed by "(The antiphon is repeated)".

Antiphon 2, artifact page 42, has the same construction: an ICEL antiphon of
three sense lines, the assignment "(Psalm 46[47]: GR, p. 140)", the same rubric,
the heading "Psalm 46", and the whole psalm in four strophes.

Psalms 23(24) and 46(47) are two of the three the file's own copyright page
reserves to The Revised Grail Psalms, Conception Abbey/The Grail, administered
by GIA Publications. ICEL's standing web permission does not reach them and this
project holds nothing from GIA. So the ICEL antiphon on each page may be
published and the psalm strophes beneath it may not, and no schema that assigns
one rights token per proper can say that. Carry the antiphon, leave the psalm,
record the split.

TWO TRAPS SIT WITH THIS ONE. The red assignment in parentheses is a CITATION and
carries no Grail text; it is the compiler's Graduale reference and is not the
thing at issue. And a second official document prints these very psalms with no
Grail notice at all -- the CBCEW Liturgy Office's Lords-Entrance.pdf, registered
at
artifact.catholic-church.missale-romanum.2011-english-cbcew-excerpts.lords-entrance-pdf,
carries only ICEL and Revised Standard Version notices while printing Psalm 23
and Psalm 46 entire. Two conference-published documents, the same psalms,
different attribution. A rights position may not be inferred from whether a
notice appears on the file in hand.
passages.notes: Located by enumerating every line matching a centred "Psalm N" heading across all 265 pages of the retained bytes: there are exactly three, at artifact pages 41, 42 and 242, and they are exactly the three psalms the copyright page reserves. passages.context:
Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord, Third Form: The Simple Entrance, the
Entrance Antiphon. Read on 2026-08-21 from the retained bytes, artifact page 44,
printed page 36. No liturgical text is transcribed into this record.

THE HARDER CASE OF THE GRAIL CARVE-OUT, and the reason the carve-out cannot be
handled by refusing a page. The antiphon is cited on its own line as
"Cf. Jn 12: 1, 12-13; Ps 23: 9-10", and it runs thirteen lines, of which the
first six are the Johannine antiphon proper and the next five are Psalm 23:9-10
-- word for word the same rendering printed under the "Psalm 23" heading at
artifact page 41, where the file's copyright page assigns it to The Revised
Grail Psalms. The psalm verses are not appended beneath the antiphon here; they
are inside it, between two repetitions of its refrain.

So the unit of rights is smaller than the slot, and on this slot it is smaller
than the sentence. Nothing here says what the answer is. It says that the
question is live on this antiphon, that it is not answerable by a per-proper
token, and that the antiphon must not land until it can be answered. The
alternative danger is symmetrical and just as real: withholding the whole slot
would withhold ICEL text that ICEL permits, on account of five lines that are
somebody else's.

The same page also carries the Second Form: The Solemn Entrance, which prints no
text of its own and directs the reader to the antiphon Hosanna and the responsory
As the Lord entered -- a cross-reference, and an example of a slot that must be
modelled as a reference rather than recorded as an absence.
passages.notes: One of four Palm Sunday loci in this file touching the Grail psalms; the other three are the two procession antiphons at artifact pages 41-42 and, distinct from them, nothing else. Psalm 115(116), the third reserved psalm, is printed entire only at artifact page 242, in the Rite of Blessing a Chalice and a Paten -- see the sibling passage. Everywhere else in this document Psalm 115 appears as a red Graduale assignment or as the ICEL antiphon at Ps 115:15 and Ps 115:12-13, which are Missal antiphons and ICEL's.

places, and they are exactly those three psalms: Psalm 23 at artifact page 41,
Psalm 46 at artifact page 42, Psalm 115 at artifact page 242. A fourth locus is
subtler: at artifact page 44 the Palm Sunday Simple Entrance Antiphon is cited
"Cf. Jn 12: 1, 12-13; Ps 23: 9-10" and prints those verses INSIDE the antiphon,
in the same wording as page 41. So the unit of rights is smaller than the slot.
A psalm CITATION in red -- the Graduale assignments printed throughout -- is not
Grail text and carries no such problem. PRINTED STROPHES on those pages are
outside this basis; carry the ICEL antiphon and not the Grail verse, and record
the split.

THE FILE. The Liturgy Office publishes it free and entire, and its Missal pages
carry "(c) CBCEW" with a grant limited to local parish use, which does not reach
a permanent website; condition (4) of ICEL's clause independently grants no
licence to publish in another form. So the exact bytes are identified and hashed
and no payload is retained: storage = remote. That disposes of the file. It
withholds nothing of the ICEL text, which is publishable under the clause above.

src/sources/inventories/icel-web-permission-rights-v1.toml settles the question
once for every later lane.
